body.x: Landfill walk or Recycling Unit Visit, as per the age of students and batch size.
Since taking under age students to a landfill is hazardous for their health; similarly, safety is a consideration to go to a landfill with a large number of students.

Delhi generates about 9,500 tonnes of waste per day, of which 8,000 tonnes is deposited at the three infamous landfills – Bhalaswa, Okhla and Ghazipur. The landfills after reaching their capacities a few years back have now been overflowing with waste dumped over them every day.

Standing in front of one, brings us face to face, literally and figuratively, to the waste menace. Students see that the chips packet or the coke bottle they threw away a few days earlier, without a single thought of where it’ll end up, is now in front of them with the other trash.

Along with trash familiar to them, they also observe people mounting up on these mountains of trash, oblivious of the filth and stench; they search through waste to look for recyclable material. These people are rag pickers – a community of people who clean up the trash we throw out mindfully. Our waste is their wealth.

A visit to a recycling facility will demonstrate to the students how different kinds of waste, primarily plastic, are recycled. It begins with segregation into various groups, the segregated waste goes through processes to become raw material again. This visit will make them realise the benefits of recycling, how it reduces the amount of waste sent to landfills and incinerators, prevents pollution by reducing the need to collect new raw materials and saves energy.

Meanwhile, emphasis will also be laid on the fact that, though recycling is a good option it is not the solution or alternative, as a significant amount of energy is spent in the process, and our efforts should always be aimed at reducing our consumption, and re-using.
